name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,240

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rubenesque in the rear, in turn sharply cut at the middle

indicators.note: the first piece is placed in the second, sitting inside its letters
a word cut at its middle loses its second half, leaving only the front

blocks.note: aft means at the back, especially of a ship
to zigzag is to turn sharply one way then the other

explanation.surface: A plump Rubens figure seen from behind, chopped through the middle by some sharp turn.
explanation.walkthrough: Halving the word for a sharp turn leaves its first part, which then takes the rear piece inside after its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Zaftig, from Yiddish, describes a pleasingly plump, curvy woman like those Rubens painted.

clue.text: Opening in one way not a thing to start on perhaps

blocks.note: zip is slang for nothing at all
to start from the top is to begin at the start

explanation.surface: Someone is told the opening move is not the thing to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: A zip-top is a can or bag opened by pulling a strip, which is the 'one way' of opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A ziptop is a particular kind of container lid or closure that can be pulled open.

clue.text: Soak once in pool, quietly going about, freezing point outside

indicators.note: something going leaves, so the quiet letter departs from the word for a pool
the abbreviation is set outside, wrapping around everything else

blocks.note: f.p. is the abbreviation for freezing point
a puddle is a small pool of water
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
ca, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A drunk lies in a pool going cold, quiet and surrounded by frost.
explanation.walkthrough: A soak is a heavy drinker. The two letters of the freezing-point abbreviation split to wrap round everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuddlecap is an obsolete word for a habitual drunkard, someone always fuddled with drink.

clue.text: One waits initially for Frenchwoman to fill kettle, possibly

indicators.note: initially points to only the opening letter of the word before it
one piece fills the gap between the others, going inside them

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Mme, Madame, is the French title for a married woman
the first letter of waits

explanation.surface: Someone stands waiting for a Frenchwoman to fill the kettle for tea.
explanation.walkthrough: To kettle is to hem protesters in, police-style, which is why 'kettle' is a verb here, and the 'possibly' admits it is one example of confining.
explanation.definitionFit: Immew is an old verb meaning to shut up or confine, as a hawk in its mew, much like kettling a crowd.

clue.text: Recalled a short school vacation, having to sunbathe in Indian house

indicators.note: a short word is clipped, losing its final letter
having means holding, so one word is held inside the other
recalled means called back, so the whole is read from the end

blocks.note: taken as written
hols is British slang for school holidays
to bask is to lie in the sun

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a brief school break spent sunbathing in an Indian house.
explanation.walkthrough: Hols is British slang for school holidays. The reversal covers the whole build, so assemble everything first and then read it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lok Sabha is the lower chamber, the House of the People, of the Indian parliament.

clue.text: Vote in noble men, disposed to be universally kind

indicators.note: disposed means arranged or set out, so the letters are laid out afresh

blocks.note: the fourteen letters used as the raw material

explanation.surface: An appeal to elect aristocrats who are inclined to be generous to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnibenevolent, a term from theology, means all-good, wishing well to every being without exception.

clue.text: Sally’s taking time out, rounding up quiz’s regulars for rising Mexican artist

indicators.note: something taken out is removed from the word it was in
regulars means letters at regular intervals, every other one
to round something is to go around it, enclosing it
in a down entry rising means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: a sally is a sortie, a sudden charge out by troops
T is the abbreviation for time
the first, third and fifth letters of these words

explanation.surface: Sally takes a break, collects the quiz regulars, and goes off to see a rising Mexican painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters are taken across two words, 'up quiz', so 'up' is not a direction here; 'rising' does that job for the whole build.
explanation.definitionFit: David Alfaro Siqueiros was a Mexican muralist, one of the big three with Rivera and Orozco.

clue.text: Brush perhaps with law at first turning to judge’s volunteer enforcers

indicators.note: at first points to only the opening letter of the word before it
turning to means changing into, so one letter becomes another

blocks.note: Basil Brush is a fox puppet from British children's television
the first letter of law
J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: A brush with the law that ends up before a judge's band of volunteer enforcers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brush' looks like a scrape with the law; it is Basil Brush, a fox puppet famous on British TV, and swapping the L of BASIL for J gives BASIJ.
explanation.definitionFit: The Basij is an Iranian paramilitary volunteer militia used to police morals and suppress protest.

clue.text: Mark is running in trousers: they won’t support his legs

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket something, so one piece is tucked inside another

blocks.note: to run someone in is slang for to arrest them
M is the abbreviation for the German mark

explanation.surface: Mark goes jogging in his trousers, which give no help to his legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' looks like clothing but is a verb meaning pockets. The definition is a joke: armrests support arms, not legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Armrests are the parts of a chair on which a seated person rests the arms, not the legs.

clue.text: Drink to pay for: support measuring system

blocks.note: a slug is a gulp of strong drink
to foot the bill is to pay it
to second a motion is to support it

explanation.surface: Someone orders a drink to pay for, and calls for backing.
explanation.definitionFit: The slug-foot-second system is a set of engineering units using the slug for mass, foot for length and second for time.

clue.text: Aussie bounder played on maiden’s vacillating

indicators.note: vacillating means wavering back and forth, so the letters move unsteadily into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: An Australian cad toys with a hesitant young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' looks like a cad, but here it is literally an animal that bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A pademelon or padymelon is a small Australian wallaby, a hopping marsupial of the scrub and forest.

clue.text: Following one back, His Majesty arrives at Iranian island

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: seq., sequens, is the abbreviation for the following one
HM is the abbreviation for His Majesty

explanation.surface: The king arrives at an island in Iran with an attendant trailing behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Qeshm is the largest island in the Persian Gulf, lying in the Strait of Hormuz off Iran.

clue.text: Friend to bear down — head to the back

indicators.note: the leading letter is moved to the end of the word

blocks.note: low means down in spirits

explanation.surface: Someone tells a friend to bear down, head bowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear down' looks like a phrase; 'bear' belongs with 'Friend to' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Owl is one of Winnie-the-Pooh's companions in A. A. Milne's stories about the bear.

clue.text: Possible source of snag developing from bite, eg in jaw

indicators.note: something developing from material grows into a new form, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the eleven letters used as raw material

explanation.surface: A snag, like a tooth problem, starting from a bite in the jaw.
explanation.walkthrough: A snag here is a catch on clothing: this South African thorn bush hooks passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: Wag-'n-bietjie, Afrikaans for wait-a-bit, is a thorny shrub whose hooked spines catch on clothing.

clue.text: Stage door that is closed after game

indicators.note: after says the word for closed comes following the word for game

blocks.note: sc., scilicet, is Latin for that is to say
RU is rugby union
a door pushed to is closed

explanation.surface: The stage door is shut once the match is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A scruto is a theatre trapdoor made of strips, a door set in the stage through which actors appear.

clue.text: Ruining in the past a branch of the family?

blocks.note: first meaning: an obsolete word for destroying or undoing
second meaning, whimsical: the side of the family belonging to a parent's brother

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second meaning as a pun: split it UNCLE WING.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclew was to unwind or undo, so unclewing once meant bringing to ruin.

clue.text: One bent on self-study returning home, crossing Bow Street

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read in the opposite direction
crossing means spanning across, so the word stretches round the next

blocks.note: at home means in
a bow is a curve or arc
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A student heads home, crossing Bow Street in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow Street is a famous London address, home of the old magistrates' court, but here Bow and Street are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcist, or narcissist, is absorbed in admiring and contemplating their own self.

clue.text: Yours truly to follow, being old and fully stretched

blocks.note: yours truly is the setter, so I
next means following
ens is the philosophical term for being or existence
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: The writer is next in line, being old and exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: In extenso is a Latin phrase meaning at full length, in full, without abridgement.

clue.text: Sheltering in Perth in Ashes venue, none leaving, none departing

indicators.note: the second nothing departs, removed from the word for leaving

blocks.note: the Sydney Cricket Ground hosts Ashes Tests between England and Australia
none is O, nought; leaving is going

explanation.surface: Sheltering from Perth's weather at an Ashes ground, with nobody leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perth' looks Australian among the Ashes talk, but it is the Scottish town, flagging a Scots word. O goes in SCG; GOING without O follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Scog is a Scots verb meaning to shelter or shade, so scogging is taking shelter.

clue.text: Catch Young Conservative, coming from the Right, cheers echoing?

indicators.note: coming from the right means read from right to left, backwards

blocks.note: to cop is to catch
YC is the abbreviation for Young Conservative
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: A young Tory, from the political right, is caught amid echoing cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Right' looks like politics for the Young Conservative; it is the direction to read TA.
explanation.definitionFit: A copycat action imitates another, so it repeats what came before, as an echo does.

clue.text: Revolutionary ideas I’ve partially endorsed

indicators.note: partially means only part of the words is used, a run of their letters
something revolutionary turns round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a run of letters straddling these words

explanation.surface: A writer claims to have half-backed some radical ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport that has been visaed has been stamped with an official approval to enter.

clue.text: Was modelling younger head of ancient goddess in wood?

indicators.note: head of means only the leading letter of the following word

blocks.note: a model sits for an artist
yr is the abbreviation for younger
the first letter of ancient

explanation.surface: A younger sitter posed as an ancient goddess carved in wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in wood' suggests a carving, but means living in a forest; the question mark admits a satyra is no true goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyra is a female satyr, a woodland deity of classical myth who roams the forests.

clue.text: One promoting growth that’s short blathering about several inches

indicators.note: a short word is clipped, losing its final letter
about means around, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: gibbering is talking nonsense
an ell is an old cloth measure of 45 inches

explanation.surface: A babbling grower who talks a lot, running over by a few inches.
explanation.walkthrough: The ell is an old cloth measure, which is why 'several inches' can stand for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibberellin is a plant hormone that stimulates stem elongation and other growth.

clue.text: Not allowed to have a single name hurt, previously

indicators.note: keeping a single copy of a doubled letter means removing the other one

blocks.note: banned means prohibited
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone forbidden to use only one name was hurt in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: To bane was an old verb meaning to poison or harm, so baned once meant injured.

clue.text: Man regularly taking to north’s provinces

indicators.note: in a down entry going to the north means reading upwards

blocks.note: IOM is the Isle of Man
someone on a medicine takes it regularly

explanation.surface: A man regularly heading north to the provinces.
explanation.walkthrough: IOM plus ON, read upwards, gives NOMOI.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomoi is the plural of nomos, an administrative department or province of Greece.

clue.text: Scots brace themselves, winter approaching: the earliest signs

indicators.note: earliest signs are the first characters of each of the preceding words

blocks.note: the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Scots steel themselves as winter draws near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brace themselves' reads as a phrase, but 'brace' means a pair and belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Twa is the Scots form of two, and a brace means a pair.

clue.text: Test team moving up the order a US Rastafarian

indicators.note: a letter moves earlier in the sequence, rearranging the team name

blocks.note: India is a Test cricket side

explanation.surface: A cricket team reshuffles its batting order to include an American Rastafarian.
explanation.walkthrough: The A of INDIA moves up to second place. 'US' is not American but the pronoun us.
explanation.definitionFit: I and I is the Rastafarian expression used for we or us, stressing unity with God.

clue.text: An economy, originally in the red maybe finding future

definitions.text: in the red maybe finding future

indicators.note: done originally means done in a novel way, so the letters take an inventive new order

blocks.note: the nine letters used as raw material

explanation.surface: An economy that starts out in the red, maybe finding a future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the red' looks like debt beside 'economy', but red is wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Oenomancy is divination by wine, reading the future from its colour and behaviour.

clue.text: Perform boring joke, song and dance for food in Asia

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so one word is inserted into the other

blocks.note: a gag is a joke
to do is to perform
a song and dance is a fuss, an ado

explanation.surface: Doing a tedious comedy routine with song and dance in exchange for a meal in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull, but it means drilling into; and 'song and dance' is a single idiom for a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Gado-gado is an Indonesian salad of vegetables, egg and tofu dressed with peanut sauce.

clue.text: A Finnish company in retreat — no way out of Africa

indicators.note: something in retreat goes backwards, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: taken as written
Nokia is the Finnish telecommunications firm

explanation.surface: A Finnish firm pulls back, finding no way out of Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Aikona is a South African exclamation of refusal, meaning certainly not or no way.
